requirements.title: Project Branding
requirements.definition: The current product is presented as Project Rebuild, with BooksOnChain retained only as a conditional future platform identity.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the rendered project identity only; future DAO, governance-token, and platform functionality are not included.

requirements.title: Landing-Page Hero Content and Layout
requirements.definition: The landing-page hero must present the approved headline, supporting copy, mint call to action, referral value proposition, and readable responsive layout.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers hero copy and layout; book-cover rendering is independently adjustable and remains separate.

requirements.title: Landing-Page Book Cover Presentation
requirements.definition: The landing page must include the ebook cover at an aesthetically appropriate size while displaying the complete image without cropping or overlap.
requirements.boundary_note: Limited to landing-page cover placement and sizing; NFT-wallet and dashboard asset rendering are separate.

requirements.title: Client-Approved FAQ Content
requirements.definition: The site must provide the client-approved FAQ explaining the product, minting, referrals, prizes, payments, wallet behavior, fees, transfers, and support.
requirements.boundary_note: Owns the FAQ artifact and its copy, not the underlying payment, referral, prize, or access behaviors described by that copy.

requirements.title: About Project Rebuild Page
requirements.definition: The site must provide the approved About Project Rebuild page and its technology, process, feature, and vision copy.
requirements.boundary_note: Treated as one independently editable page artifact; underlying technical claims remain owned by their product Requirements.

requirements.title: Our Mission Page
requirements.definition: The site must provide the approved Our Mission page describing purpose, community, fair rewards, innovation, long-term vision, and current mechanics.
requirements.boundary_note: Treated as an independently editable content page rather than merged with the hero, About page, or FAQ.

requirements.title: Top-Affiliate Prize Mechanism
requirements.definition: The historical product concept awarding prizes to top affiliates is retained as a distinct prize mechanism in the observable lifecycle.
requirements.boundary_note: Kept separately because the first visible evidence removes this entire mechanism rather than modifying Small or Big Block attributes.

requirements.title: Small Block Prize Mechanism
requirements.definition: The Small Block mechanism governs its prize pool, ticket issuance and reset, eligibility, draw trigger, winner count, prize amount, random selection, and ticket accounting.
requirements.boundary_note: Winner count, prize amount, trigger, ticket reset, and ticket-routing rules are attributes of one tightly coupled draw mechanism; Big Block remains separate.

requirements.title: Big Block Prize Mechanism
requirements.definition: The Big Block mechanism governs its independent ticket counter, prize pool, eligibility window, trigger, winner selection, prize amount, and associated UI.
requirements.boundary_note: Separate from Small Block because its parameters and eventual removal evolve independently.

requirements.title: Prize Winner Claim Flow
requirements.definition: Prize winners must be able to see their win and use the conditional one-click claim interaction during the applicable claim period.
requirements.boundary_note: Claim interaction is independently testable after winner selection and is therefore separate from the Small Block draw itself.

requirements.title: Aave Prize-Pool Yield Integration
requirements.definition: Prize-pool funds may be integrated with Aave to accrue yield as an independently removable pool-infrastructure feature.
requirements.boundary_note: Aave integration can be removed without removing the underlying prize mechanism, so it is not an attribute of Small Block.

requirements.title: NFT-Owned Referral Code Identity
requirements.definition: Each NFT's permanent referral code must be its own mint number and must be surfaced consistently on the NFT, in metadata, on the dashboard, and where applicable in email.
requirements.boundary_note: Defines code ownership and display; whether a submitted code is valid is a separate validation behavior.

requirements.title: Referral Code Validation and Self-Referral Prevention
requirements.definition: A referral code is valid only when it identifies an already minted NFT, preventing buyers from using a future or self-owned mint number.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers acceptance and rejection logic only; popup wording and commission payout are separately testable.

requirements.title: Referral Validation Feedback
requirements.definition: The mint interface must clearly distinguish valid referral codes from absent or invalid codes and explain the corresponding reward recipient behavior.
requirements.boundary_note: Owns validation-result copy, not the underlying validity rule or final mint-success message.

requirements.title: Commission for Code-Based Referrals
requirements.definition: When a valid referral code is used for a mint, the selected NFT holder must receive the configured commission automatically and have it attributed to that NFT.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers commission payout for an explicit code; prize tickets and no-code random allocation have separate trajectories.

requirements.title: Random Commission Allocation Without a Referral Code
requirements.definition: A mint without a referral code must allocate its commission to a randomly selected existing NFT holder, with a defined one-off exception when no earlier NFT exists.
requirements.boundary_note: Commission allocation is separate from the Small Block ticket because the two were observed to fail and recover independently.

requirements.title: Unlimited Primary NFT Ebook Mint
requirements.definition: Buyers must be able to mint the ebook as an unlimited-supply NFT and receive a distinct token representing ownership of the book.
requirements.boundary_note: Defines the minted product and supply model; currency-specific execution paths and price are separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Primary Mint Price
requirements.definition: The primary ebook NFT mint must use the client-confirmed fixed price and communicate that price accurately in the interface and product copy.
requirements.boundary_note: Price can change independently of how the proceeds are allocated, so the revenue split is separate.

requirements.title: Primary Sale Revenue Allocation
requirements.definition: Each primary sale must allocate the mint proceeds among the founder, affiliate commission, and active prize pool according to the client-confirmed split.
requirements.boundary_note: Owns the economic split; recipient selection and actual commission attribution remain under referral Requirements.

requirements.title: USDC Wallet Mint Flow
requirements.definition: A connected-wallet buyer must be able to approve USDC spending and complete the NFT mint, with success recorded only after the mint transaction succeeds.
requirements.boundary_note: USDC approval and auto-mint have an execution trajectory independent of ETH conversion and fiat-card checkout.

requirements.title: ETH Wallet Mint and Conversion Flow
requirements.definition: A connected-wallet buyer must be able to pay with ETH, obtain the required mint-price amount through the configured swap, receive any excess in the approved refund currency, and receive the NFT.
requirements.boundary_note: ETH conversion, pricing, refund, and swap failures are independent of the USDC approval flow and therefore remain separate.

requirements.title: Transak Fiat Mint Integration
requirements.definition: The product must support a Transak-based card and mobile-pay fiat on-ramp that converts payment to crypto and initiates the NFT mint for non-crypto buyers.
requirements.boundary_note: Provider selection and fiat checkout are separate from background wallet provisioning and later reward access.

requirements.title: Background Wallet Provisioning for Fiat Buyers
requirements.definition: A fiat buyer without an existing wallet must receive a non-custodial wallet in the background without an initial seed-phrase setup burden.
requirements.boundary_note: Wallet creation is independently testable from Transak checkout and from the user's later dashboard access to rewards.

requirements.title: Fiat Buyer Access to Commissions and Prizes
requirements.definition: Non-crypto fiat buyers must be able to access their provisioned wallet, NFT, commissions, tickets, prizes, and related guidance through the dashboard and email flow.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers post-purchase reward access, not wallet creation or the card transaction itself.

requirements.title: Optional Mint Tipping
requirements.definition: The mint page must offer preset and custom optional tips, execute the tip transparently as a separate transfer when required, and prevent invalid founder self-tipping.
requirements.boundary_note: Tipping is optional and independently executable after minting, so it is not part of the fixed mint price or revenue split.

requirements.title: Accurate Mint Success Confirmation
requirements.definition: The success modal must appear only after the relevant mint and reward-finalization operations succeed, show the correct token ID, and use scenario-specific referral or no-referral copy.
requirements.boundary_note: Confirmation timing and copy can fail while the underlying mint succeeds, so this is separate from USDC and ETH execution.

requirements.title: Wallet Authentication for Crypto Flows
requirements.definition: Crypto users must be able to authenticate through wallet-based Sign-In with Ethereum for wallet-dependent product flows.
requirements.boundary_note: Wallet authentication can evolve independently of email dashboard access and unauthenticated public APIs.

requirements.title: Email and Magic-Link Dashboard Authentication
requirements.definition: Users without wallets must be able to authenticate to the dashboard through a simple email-based flow such as magic links, with verified-email state handled correctly.
requirements.boundary_note: Owns identity and session access; general transactional email delivery is a separate service behavior.

requirements.title: Unauthenticated Public API Access
requirements.definition: Public data such as leaderboards and prize-pool values must remain accessible through unauthenticated APIs.
requirements.boundary_note: Public API access is independent of wallet and email authentication used for private user functions.

requirements.title: Pinata IPFS Ebook Storage
requirements.definition: The ebook PDF must be stored through Pinata/IPFS in a way that supports the client's desired content-control and integration workflow.
requirements.boundary_note: Storage location and removability are separate from Lit-based access control and reader presentation.

requirements.title: NFT-Holder Ebook Access Gating
requirements.definition: The ebook must be encrypted and accessible only after the system verifies ownership of a valid Project Rebuild NFT through Lit Protocol.
requirements.boundary_note: Owns authorization and decryption; PDF navigation and mobile-wallet compatibility have independent execution trajectories.

requirements.title: Read-Only Ebook Reader
requirements.definition: Authorized NFT holders must be able to read the PDF through the integrated viewer with functional page navigation and usable controls.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers reader rendering and navigation after access is granted; ownership verification and offline download are separate.

requirements.title: Mobile Wallet Ebook Access
requirements.definition: NFT holders using supported mobile wallet applications must be able to complete the required signing and decryption flow and open the ebook reader.
requirements.boundary_note: Mobile wallet handoff can fail while desktop access works, establishing an independent execution path.

requirements.title: Optional Offline PDF Download
requirements.definition: The ebook access experience must provide an optional, secondary PDF download path for offline reading in addition to the default read-only viewer.
requirements.boundary_note: Offline download is independently selectable and is not an attribute of reader navigation.

requirements.title: NFT Certificate and Read-Link Email
requirements.definition: A successful buyer must be able to receive an NFT certificate email containing the prominent read action and relevant NFT and referral information.
requirements.boundary_note: The certificate is a distinct delivered artifact; general email transport remains under transactional email delivery.

requirements.title: Accurate Dashboard NFT Listing
requirements.definition: The dashboard must list the NFTs actually owned by the connected user and must not show failed, duplicate, missing, or unrelated mints.
requirements.boundary_note: Owns whether the correct tokens are listed; asset images and reward values are separately testable.

requirements.title: Accurate Dashboard Reward Summary
requirements.definition: The user dashboard must accurately display owned tickets, referrals, commissions, earnings, prize-pool participation, and earned badges.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the owner-level dashboard summary; leaderboard totals and per-NFT metadata attributes are separate views.

requirements.title: Accurate Referral Leaderboard
requirements.definition: The leaderboard must accurately attribute and total referrals, tickets, and commission earnings for each NFT, including randomly assigned no-code rewards.
requirements.boundary_note: The leaderboard is an independently failing projection of reward state, not the reward-allocation mechanism itself.

requirements.title: Accurate Public Platform Statistics
requirements.definition: Public and home-page statistics must accurately report total supply, mint count, prize-pool value, next mint, referrals, and other aggregate product values.
requirements.boundary_note: Aggregate platform counters are separate from user-specific dashboard and per-NFT reward views.

requirements.title: NFT Transfer State Semantics
requirements.definition: When an NFT is transferred or sold, the new owner must receive the book, permanent mint-number referral code, badges, and applicable active ticket state while expired tickets remain expired.
requirements.boundary_note: Defines state that follows NFT ownership; royalty enforcement and marketplace controls are separate.

requirements.title: Secondary-Sale Royalty Enforcement
requirements.definition: Secondary marketplace sales must enforce the configured flat royalty through the client-confirmed ERC-721C marketplace-control approach and fund the applicable allocations without generating referral tickets.
requirements.boundary_note: Royalty collection and marketplace restrictions are distinct from primary mint pricing and NFT transfer-state inheritance.

requirements.title: Base Network Deployment
requirements.definition: The NFT, payment, prize, and ownership-verification system must operate on the Base network using the appropriate production configuration.
requirements.boundary_note: Base is a client-confirmed platform constraint shared across features, not a substitute for their individual behavioral Requirements.

requirements.title: Smart-Contract Migration and State Continuity
requirements.definition: Contract replacements or upgrades must follow the client-approved migration approach and preserve existing users, NFTs, and data whenever continuity is required.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a migration-specific data obligation, not generic deployment or project scheduling.

requirements.title: Badge Grid and Responsive Presentation
requirements.definition: The badge interface must present the approved badge set in a balanced, responsive layout on desktop and mobile.
requirements.boundary_note: Layout can fail while badge eligibility remains correct, establishing a separate presentation Requirement.

requirements.title: Mauritius Landing-Page Geoblock
requirements.definition: Access to the Project Rebuild landing page must be geoblocked for users located in Mauritius.
requirements.boundary_note: Geographic access control is independent of payment-provider availability in the business's incorporation country.

requirements.title: Production Website Availability
requirements.definition: The deployed Project Rebuild application must remain reachable and functional in production without gateway or failed-deployment outages.
requirements.boundary_note: Availability is an independently observable runtime constraint and does not duplicate failures of individual mint or reader behaviors.

requirements.title: Wallet and Browser Trust-Warning Remediation
requirements.definition: The project must complete the applicable developer-verification and false-positive reporting steps to remove or prevent malicious-site warnings during access.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a specific trust-registration remediation task, not a generic security or testing Requirement.

requirements.title: Production Contract-Event Webhook
requirements.definition: The backend must receive Base Mainnet contract logs through an authenticated Alchemy webhook and route relevant mint, referral, and ticket events by signature.
requirements.boundary_note: This is an independently configured event-ingestion interface; downstream reward accounting remains owned by its product Requirements.

requirements.title: Mint Number One Ownership Assignment
requirements.definition: The client must receive ownership of the NFT carrying mint and affiliate code number one at the specified wallet.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a one-off state-changing transfer obligation, not a general NFT transfer policy.

requirements.title: Landing-Page Support Contact Form
requirements.definition: The site must provide a help or contact entry point with the approved user details and inquiry fields for support, questions, and suggestions.
requirements.boundary_note: The on-site support form is an independent product interface and is not merged with the external Discord community.

requirements.title: Project Rebuild Discord Community Server
requirements.definition: The project must provide a configured Discord community with onboarding, announcements, feedback, support, bug-reporting, product, roadmap, and voice channels.
requirements.boundary_note: Discord configuration is an independently delivered operational system, distinct from the website contact form.

requirements.title: Landing-Page How It Works Section Content
requirements.definition: The landing page must present the client-approved copy for the independently editable How It Works section.
requirements.boundary_note: Changed by consistency audit.

requirements.title: Payment Method Selection and Currency Disclosure
requirements.definition: The mint interface must identify the currency being used, allow selection among implemented alternatives, and prevent selection of unavailable payment methods.
requirements.boundary_note: Owns checkout choice and disclosure; successful execution of each payment path belongs to its currency-specific Requirement.

requirements.title: Payment Method Availability Gating

requirements.title: Brevo Transactional Email Transport
requirements.definition: Brevo-backed transactional emails must be delivered with accurate mint, referral, badge, prize, and other user-notification content.

requirements.title: Accurate Badge Email Notifications

requirements.title: Achievement Badge Award Rules

requirements.title: Accurate NFT Metadata Reward Attributes
requirements.definition: Each NFT's detail view and generated metadata must accurately expose that NFT's referrals, tickets, commissions, earnings, and related live reward attributes.
requirements.boundary_note: Limited to reward attributes; the NFT's own referral-code identity and media assets are owned by separate Requirements.

requirements.title: NFT Asset Presentation in Wallets and Product Views
requirements.definition: Minted NFTs must resolve and display their image, metadata, and book links correctly in supported wallets, the dashboard, and NFT detail views.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hero copy: A dropout multimillionaire went to zero because of one oversight. Now rebuilding through an eBook model designed to free creators from Amazon's 70% cut.

Supporting headline: “My Underdog Journey: To Own Goal” — an unlimited NFT book on Base, priced at $15 forever.

Mechanics preview: Buy → own the book and receive your referral link. Refer → earn an instant $5 with no limit, plus 1 entry into a random $500 giveaway every 100 sales.

CTA text: Mint the eBook NFT for $15

Make $500 Every 100 Sales Prominent: Revise all relevant copy so the frequency is the main motivator, using language such as “constant small shots at $500.”

For the prize area: “Win $500 every 100 sales — every referral earns 1 ticket, with a fair drawing through Chainlink VRF. More referrals mean more chances!”

Also include this in the mechanics preview: “Refer to receive an instant $5 and your chance at $500 every 100 sales.”
The experience should feel like an “ongoing roulette spin” for hustlers.

Add these FAQs:
How Can a Non-Crypto Fiat Buyer Receive Commissions and Prizes?
If you're new to crypto and paying with fiat, such as a credit card, Apple Pay, etc., don't worry — the flow is intended to be straightforward. When the book is minted for $15 through Transak, a non-custodial wallet is created automatically in the background, without requiring a seed phrase initially. That wallet stores the NFT and receives all commissions and prizes. The steps are below:

At Purchase:
Transak converts the fiat into crypto and mints the NFT directly to a newly created wallet address. There is nothing for you to configure manually — the experience is seamless and non-custodial. You control the keys, without having to manage a complicated seed phrase right away.
An email confirmation will provide your mint number, which is also your referral code, along with the NFT information and a link to your dashboard at [URL_002].

Receiving Commissions ($5 per Referral):
Share your referral code, for example, “use 8421.” Whenever another person mints using it, $5 is transferred automatically to your wallet address.
To access it, sign in to the dashboard at [URL_002], either from the email link or through SIWE with the wallet created by Transak. The commissions appear immediately, with no additional action required.

Earning and Receiving Prizes:
Every referral automatically provides a ticket for the active prize drawing, tied to your NFT and wallet.
The on-chain drawings award $500 every 100 sales using fair randomness. Winners are posted on the Winners page and notified by email.
If you win, the $500 goes directly to your wallet. Look at the dashboard for the notification; we'll also email step-by-step guidance for viewing it or claiming it in fiat if necessary, such as a link to a simple exchange guide. A seed phrase is not required; use the dashboard for access.

How Can Beginners Collect Their Commissions and Prizes?
If this is new to you, don't worry — the process is automatic and simple to monitor. Here is the step-by-step flow:

Receiving Commissions ($5 per Referral):
When another person mints the book with your referral code — your mint number shown in the dashboard or confirmation email — $5 is delivered to your wallet instantly. You do not have to take any action because the smart contract manages it.

Receiving Prize Tickets:
Each completed referral additionally awards 1 ticket for the $500 prize held every 100 sales. The ticket is added to your NFT automatically and can be viewed in the dashboard.
No action is necessary; each ticket is on-chain and associated with your mint number.

Winning and Receiving Prizes:
Once a pool reaches its trigger every 100 sales, Chainlink VRF, a fair random system, runs the drawing automatically. Winners appear on the Winners page and are notified by email if they supplied one.
A winner receives $500 in their wallet immediately. Check the dashboard for alerts; we'll send an email as well.
Tickets expire once their applicable drawing is complete, while new referrals award tickets for the following blocks.

Additional Copy Adjustments:
Mechanics List: Center every item on the frequent opportunities to win $500 and the accompanying $5 commission, reinforcing the idea of “cut middlemen, funnel savings.”

Prize Section: Replace the current explanation that the pool reaches $500 every 100 sales and 1 winner is randomly chosen from all ticket holders through Chainlink VRF for provably fair randomness. The replacement should say: “**$500 every 100 sales!** 1 affiliate is chosen from that 100 sales block through Chainlink VRF for provably fair randomness. **More referrals = more chances to win!**” Make this the headline so it stands out when skimming.

General: Replace “revolutionary” with “aligned” or “fair” to reduce the hype and emphasize the ethos. Under the stats, add the tagline “Help the rebuild — share to earn.”

Visual/UI Adjustments:
Place the book cover in the hero and integrate it with the headline.
Use “Mint your eBook” / “Mint your eBook NFT.”
Live Counters: Include “Next $500 Draw In: ~X Sales” to create urgency.
Mobile Test: Confirm that the stats and mechanics stack correctly without anything being cut off.

Page Title: About Project Rebuild
Sub-title: The first ebook launch that pays readers to spread it.

What is Project Rebuild?
Project Rebuild serves as the live proof-of-concept for FAMM (Fully Autonomous Marketing Model) — the first system that allows indie creators to sell NFT ebooks with unlimited minting and reward readers with real commissions + prize tickets for sharing them.
It is launching on Base with my own raw memoir novella, "My Underdog Journey: To Own Goal,".
It is also my public mission to rebuild my family's life after a seed-phrase wipeout caused us to lose millions.

If our FAMM proves itself here, Project Rebuild will become BooksOnChain — a community-owned public good platform for every creator.

Built with Cutting-Edge Technology

- Smart Contracts
Secure, audited Solidity on Base.
- Chainlink VRF
Random prize-draw selection that is provably fair.
- Aave Integration
Deposits allow the prize pools to generate yield.
- Base Network
Fast transactions and low fees, supported by Ethereum security.
- Decentralized
All logic is fully on-chain from day one, while V1 includes initial safeguards.
(battle-testing will guide the evolution to full decentralization)

- Secure
Uses industry-leading protocols and best practices.

The Process

Mint the ebook NFT
Buy your ebook NFT for $15 USD. The mint number you receive becomes your referral code.

Earn Through Referrals
Share either your mint number or your link. Whenever someone mints with it, you immediately earn $5 USD. There are no limits and no expiration.
If no code is provided → the $5 + tickets are awarded to a random existing ticket holder.

Build Up Tickets
Every referral also awards you Small & Big Block prize tickets for the current blocks.
More referrals = more tickets = greater chances.

Enter the Prize Draws
Small Block: 5 × $500 awarded every 500 sales.
Big Block: 5 × $10,000 awarded every 50,000 sales.
(Sales = mint + secondary)
Chainlink VRF selects the winners randomly and fairly.

Receive Your Rewards
Commissions are delivered automatically on-chain. Prize wins are posted on the Winners page and can be claimed with one click whenever you're ready.

Key Features

Automatic Rewards: Smart contracts issue all payments instantly.
Fair Prize Selection: Chainlink VRF provides genuine randomness.
Yield Generation: Aave Integration enables the prize pools to accrue yield.
Gamification: Badges and leaderboards keep the experience fun and competitive.
Transparency: Every transaction and rule is on-chain and verifiable.
Low Fees: Base provides speed with minimal transaction costs.

Our Vision
Project Rebuild begins with one book, but that is only the start.
We imagine a world where ebooks succeed solely on merit, free from gatekeepers and Amazon algorithms that drown out indie voices.
In that world, creators (unknown or established) rise because their work connects with people, not because they game a platform, have the connections, or purchase enough ads.
Fans are paid for the word-of-mouth marketing they have always provided for free, while any hustler can jump in and earn after spotting a gem worth spreading.

Our goal is a self-sustaining model that benefits everyone.
Artists receive their fair share, fans & affiliates develop real income, and communities build direct bonds — turning one underdog's recovery into a decentralized revolution for all creators.
All without hype, driven only by aligned incentives.

Project Rebuild isn't merely an ebook launch — it's a movement focused on repairing what is broken in publishing.

Community First

We trust in what a community can accomplish. Each member's success contributes to collective growth, transforming personal wins into momentum shared by everyone.

Fair Rewards
Unlimited, transparent, on-chain rewards make sure everyone receives what they deserve. There are no hidden terms and no middlemen.

Innovation
We're extending the boundaries of NFT, smart contracts, and decentralized technology. We will start by proving our FAMM, with the goal of becoming a full DAO after momentum builds.

Long-Term Vision
We're creating something sustainable that delivers real impact. This is a long-term effort to produce lasting value, scaling from one underdog story into a platform for everyone.

Referral Rewards: Receive $5 for every person you successfully refer to the project. Expand the network and increase your rewards.
Prize Pools: Small Block (5 × $500 every 500 sales) and Big Block (5 × $10,000 every 50,000 sales) use Chainlink VRF randomness to give referrers a fair opportunity to secure big wins.
Gamification: Badges, leaderboards, and achievement make the experience engaging and enjoyable while recognizing and rewarding active community members.
Transparency: All activity takes place on-chain. Smart contracts provide fair play and automated payouts.

Join the Movement
Become part of a community where your contributions are valued and your success is rewarded.

Hey [FREELANCER_NAME_001],
I have one final-final adjustment to the mechanics that should make everything cleaner and easier to code, without any strange half-expiring tickets.
This new rule replaces the earlier ticket lifespan description:
→ Whenever someone mints using a referral code, the referrer immediately receives two distinct tickets on their NFT:
+1 Small Block Ticket
+1 Big Block Ticket

The two counters operate completely independently.
Small Block ($2,500 pool → 5 × $500 draw):
Only Small Block Tickets issued after the previous small block are eligible for the draw.
Once the draw is complete, burn/reset every Small Block Ticket to 0.
Big Block ($100,000 pool → 5 × $20,000 draw):
Only Big Block Tickets issued after the previous big block are eligible for the draw.
Once the draw is complete, burn/reset every Big Block Ticket to 0.

The result is:
Small blocks remain extremely fair and fresh because no old tickets carry over.
Big blocks build up naturally, allowing people to watch their big block entries increase over weeks/months.
Metadata becomes very simple: display only the two counters plus permanent badges.

The triggers remain pool-based: the small block activates as soon as the small pool = exactly $2,500, and the big block activates when the big pool = exactly $100,000. Secondary royalties continue to fund the pools but do not generate tickets.
All other mechanics remain unchanged, including the auto $5 commission, assigning a random ticket to an existing NFT when no referral is used, manual claim, etc.
This approach should be simpler both to implement and to explain to users.
Apologies for changing direction again — once you confirm that this is cleaner for you as well, we’re 100% locked.

Thanks man!

What does Project Rebuild involve?
Project Rebuild is my public mission to restore my family’s life after we lost everything because of a seed-phrase mistake.
I’m selling my novella memoir on Base as an unlimited-mint NFT ebook, powered by my first-of-its-kind FAMM (Fully Autonomous Marketing Model).
By sharing it, readers can earn instant, unlimited commissions & prizes. If the model succeeds, it will become BooksOnChain — a community-owned platform serving every indie creator.

How can buyers make money?
1. Receive an instant $5 commission whenever somebody mints with your referral code
2. Earn Small & Big Block prize tickets each time a person mints using your code
3. Receive the future BooksOnChain governance token (for buyers, affiliates, and tippers)

How does the referral system operate?
The mint number of every NFT IS its permanent referral code.
Either of these examples works perfectly:
→ Share the complete link
→ Or simply tell someone “use referral 423”
When a person mints with your code, you immediately receive $5 + Small & Big Block prize tickets for the current blocks.

How can I locate my referral code?
Your referral code is your mint number. It will appear:
- In your NFT metadata on-chain
- On your Dashboard once you have minted
- In your confirmation email (optional)

### How do Small Block and Big Block prizes work?
Small Block: 5 × $500 are drawn every ~500 sales (mint + secondary)
Big Block: 5 × $10,000 are drawn every ~50,000 sales (mint + secondary)
Every sale funds the pools forever.

### How are the winners chosen?
Winners are selected through Chainlink VRF — entirely on-chain, provably fair, and verifiable on Basescan.

### What do Small & Big Block prize tickets represent?
They are one-time entries for the current Small Block and current Big Block draws.
You receive them only when people mint through your code (1 Small + 1 Big for each successful referral).
After the block is drawn, those tickets expire, and subsequent referrals apply to the next blocks.

### How can I collect my rewards?
- $5 commissions → transferred to your wallet automatically
- Prize wins → posted on the Winners page and claimable with one click here on [URL_002]

### What do badges mean?
Badges are added to your NFT on-chain when you reach referral milestones (2, 10, 50, 100+).
At present, they are cosmetic + leaderboard flex only. Later, they may provide access to token-gated chats, discounts, airdrops, DAO weight, etc.

### Can I use fiat (credit card) to mint?
Yes — Transak accepts cards, Apple Pay, and Google Pay. Neither crypto nor a wallet is required.

### Is a wallet required to participate?
Only when you want affiliate commissions paid to you or intend to trade the NFT later.

### Which blockchain does this use?
Base (Ethereum L2) — fast, inexpensive, and Coinbase-backed.

### Are hidden fees involved?
No. A mint costs exactly $15. Secondary sales include a clearly displayed flat $10 royalty.

### What occurs when I sell my NFT?
The purchaser receives the book, your original mint number (which becomes their referral code), and all badges you earned. Any expired prize tickets remain expired.

### How can I share my referral link/code?
From the Dashboard → copy the complete link, or copy only your mint number and tell people “use referral 423”.

### Is this a pyramid scheme or scam?
No. It is single-level only, the supply is unlimited, and the full source is verified on Basescan. I receive exactly $4 from every sale forever — the same cut from mints and every secondary sale.

### How can I reach support?
There is no Discord yet (it will launch after we gain real traction).
For the moment:
DM [HANDLE_001] on X
or
email [EMAIL_002]
I respond personally and quickly.

If you still have questions, DM [HANDLE_001] on X or email [EMAIL_002] — I’m happy to assist.
